description: Lists the posts and comments a Reddit account has SAVED. PRIVATE data: Reddit serves it only to the account that owns it, so the request carries that account's Reddit session cookies (the session and loid arguments, from POST /api/reddit/login on the REST API, which is not an MCP tool) and returns 403 when `name` is a different account. Mixed listing: each item is a post or a comment, tagged `kind`. Example: name='spez' (the logged-in account).

after.description: Opaque pagination cursor: the previous response's `after` value, exactly as it was returned. The format is not stable, and a hand-written Reddit fullname loses the paging depth the cursor carries. Absent on the opening page. A null `after` on a response means there is no next page; it does not by itself mean the listing is complete, because Reddit often stops serving a busy listing long before it runs out. That final response carries `listing_status`: `complete`, `truncated` or `unknown`, and only `complete` means nothing is missing.

csrf_token.description: Reddit CSRF cookie, from the same login response. Optional: a read is accepted without it (CSRF only guards state-changing calls).

limit.description: Maximum items returned, 1 to 100. The API clamps out-of-range values; the endpoint default applies when omitted.

loid.description: Reddit account loid cookie, from the same POST /api/reddit/login response. Required.

name.description: Reddit username WITHOUT the u/ prefix: the SAME account the supplied cookies belong to, or Reddit returns 403. Required (path parameter).

reddit_session.description: The Reddit account's session cookie, as returned by POST /api/reddit/login on the REST API (a REST call, not an MCP tool). Required.

sort.description: Sort order for a user's comments. 'new' = most recent (default), 'hot', 'top' (in the `t` window), 'controversial'.

t.description: Time window, only applied when sort is 'top' or 'controversial'. E.g. 'week' = top of the past week. Ignored for other sorts.

name: reddit_user_saved
